claim: A dedicated shuttle bus loops from Modena rail station (Pensilina 4) to the Maranello Ferrari Museum, ~30 min each way, with morning and afternoon departures and combined tickets around €10–11 round trip.
quote: Departure trips from Modena Railway Station at Bus Station 'PENSILLINA N°4' to Ferrari Museum in Maranello are at 10:40 and at 15:20, with return trips from Ferrari Museum in Maranello at 14:45 and 18:00.

claim: Ferrari runs two distinct museums — the Enzo Ferrari Museum in Modena and the Museo Ferrari in Maranello — sold separately or as a combined ticket.
quote: Tickets and Passes Ferrari Museums

claim: Public bus #815 from Modena's bus station reaches Maranello (IPSIA stop) in roughly 45 minutes as a cheaper alternative to the shuttle.
quote: You can take bus #815 from Modena's bus station, which will take you to the Maranello IPSIA stop.

claim: Castelvetro di Modena is the official home of Lambrusco Grasparossa DOC and lists numerous cellars open for tastings along the Strada dei Vini.
quote: Produttori di vini a Castelvetro di Modena

claim: Castelvetro carries the Italian Touring Club Orange Flag and has been certified 'City of Wine' since 1994, making it the obvious anchor village for a Lambrusco hills half-day.
quote: Castelvetro di Modena has been named 'The city of wine' since 1994 and is famous for its prestigious wine 'Lambrusco Grasparossa'.

claim: Castelvetro's signature Sagra dell'Uva e del Lambrusco Grasparossa runs across the third and fourth weekends of September with tastings, costumed parades and live music in the medieval centre.
quote: Grape and Lambrusco Grasparossa di Castelvetro Festival

claim: Vignola sits roughly 25 km south of Modena and is known nationally for its PGI Moretta cherry and the Rocca dei Contrari fortress.
quote: Vignola is located about twenty-five kilometers from Modena and is world famous for its cherries and for its splendid Rocca dei Contrari Fortress.

claim: The 'Vignola è tempo di ciliegie' cherry festival runs across two weekends spanning late May and early June 2026 — perfectly timed for a late-May Modena weekend.
quote: Vignola è tempo di ciliegie

claim: The Rocca di Vignola is one of the most important fortified buildings in Emilia, paired with Palazzo Barozzi's self-supporting 106-step spiral staircase across Piazza dei Contrari.
quote: A masterpiece of architecture of the 1500s, the staircase is a striking, self-supporting structure in the shape of a sinuous spiral with 106 steps.

claim: Carpi, ~20 km northwest of Modena and reachable by regional train in about 15 minutes, is built around Piazza dei Martiri — among the largest piazzas in Italy — and the Palazzo dei Pio museum complex.
quote: Piazza dei Martiri: 'The third largest piazza in Italy'

claim: Carpi is largely overlooked by foreign tourists and feels authentically local, with regular regional trains from Modena making it an easy half-day add-on.
quote: Carpi is a relatively unknown charming town just a 15-minute train ride from Modena.

claim: The Palazzo Ducale di Sassuolo is part of the state-run Gallerie Estensi and ranks among the most lavish Baroque summer residences in northern Italy.
quote: Palazzo Ducale - Sassuolo - Gallerie Estensi

claim: Palazzo Ducale di Sassuolo reopens 27 March 2026 with Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00 hours through 31 December 2026 and now displays 374 works from the Galleria Estense across thirteen newly restored rooms.
quote: Il Palazzo Ducale di Sassuolo riapre le porte, tra sfarzo barocco, la Pimpa e sguardi sul paesaggio

claim: The Abbey of San Silvestro at Nonantola, ~10 km from Modena, was founded in 752 AD and preserves a Wiligelmo-school portal and a crypt with 64 columns, including Lombard capitals.
quote: Abbey of San Silvestro in Nonantola

claim: Nonantola's abbey museum holds parchments and documents dating back before the year 1000 and is open daily 9:00–17:30, with a summer closure 9–25 August.
quote: San Silvestro abbey - VisitModena

claim: Direct trains link Modena and Parma roughly 20 times per day with the fastest Frecciarossa services running ~27 minutes; standard regional fares start around €7.
quote: Trains from Modena to Parma take an average of 32 minutes, although on the fastest services it can take just 27 minutes.

claim: A single day in Parma comfortably covers the Romanesque Cathedral with Correggio's dome fresco, the pink-marble Baptistery and the Palazzo della Pilotta complex with the Teatro Farnese.
quote: One day is enough to explore the highlights of Parma - you can see the main sights like the Cathedral, the Baptistery, and Palazzo della Pilotta in a day.

claim: Bologna is roughly a 30-minute regional train from Modena with ticket prices around €3–10, making it the cheapest and easiest big-city escape.
quote: You can make the journey in less than an hour, with it being only a 30-minute train ride from Bologna. Tickets for this trip range from 3 to 10 euros.

claim: A focused Bologna half-day works around Piazza Maggiore, Basilica di San Petronio, the Asinelli Tower climb and the Quadrilatero food market.
quote: If you only have a day in Bologna, start at Piazza Maggiore and visit the Basilica di San Petronio. Wander through the Quadrilatero Market to experience foodie heaven, then climb the Asinelli Tower for unparalleled views.

claim: Reggio Emilia sits 15 minutes by regional train from Modena and offers the Basilica della Ghiara, Sala del Tricolore, Teatro Valli and Calatrava's AV Mediopadana station — pleasant but with no marquee sights.
quote: Reggio Emilia is a town most tourists skip, and this charming city in Emilia Romagna is well worth a visit... You won't find top attractions here, but that's the beauty of it—everything feels local and authentic.

claim: Experienced Italy travellers on forums consistently rank Reggio Emilia third after Modena and Parma and often suggest cutting it from a tight itinerary.
quote: Bologna to Modena, Parma, & Reggio Emilia - Rick Steves Travel Forum

claim: Local food-tour operators frame Bologna, Modena and Parma as a triangle where Modena suits a calmer base and Bologna delivers the bigger urban hit if you only have one day to spare.
quote: Modena vs Bologna vs Parma: Which City Is Best for Food, Tours & Day Trips?

claim: Castelvetro and Vignola pair naturally on a single hill-country drive — only ~15 minutes apart — covering Lambrusco tastings and the Rocca in one half-day.
quote: Just 15 minutes from Castelvetro di Modena, Vignola makes for an easy and rewarding detour.
